purpose: Govern projection-source selection so predictive evidence, source independence, access cost, and intended-use rights are evaluated separately before any source becomes a production dependency.

selection_policy.accuracy_first_with_materiality: Prefer the source or blend with the best leakage-safe held-out predictive performance, but do not add cost, restrictive dependency, or material complexity for a trivial gain.
selection_policy.zero_cost_default: A paid external projection source cannot become a default FSFFL production dependency while the external projection license budget is zero.
selection_policy.rights_gate: Benchmark access, public accessibility, or open-source retrieval code does not by itself establish production, redistribution, or commercial-use rights. Intended-use rights must be verified separately before production dependency.
selection_policy.independence_gate: Only independently produced fantasy projection systems may count as independent projection-source votes. Underlying football data used to build an FSFFL-native model does not count as a second projection source.
selection_policy.native_model_preference: Prefer a simple FSFFL-native challenger built from legally usable underlying football data when it can match or materially improve held-out accuracy without paid projection licensing.
selection_policy.promotion_rule: Production promotion requires leakage-safe held-out evidence, sufficient player/position coverage, operational reliability, and intended-use rights consistent with the deployment context.

candidates.notes: Multiple dated historical preseason snapshots are already in the leakage-safe inventory. Predictive superiority and intended-use rights are not assumed.
